title: Show HN: All local LLM(s) on all Apple Devices
author: fclairamb
raw_text: Various simulation running website with complete LLM indexation support.I thought it would be interesting to explain everyone what kind of model can be run in each type of Apple Device.If I give a shared simulation like https://simulkit.com/en/mac-local-llm/6MwixMWu8mAny LLM will be able to read it because it also generates the LLM side of it: https://simulkit.com/en/mac-local-llm/6MwixMWu8m.md .Also there's no tracking, it's a PWA that works fully offline, and there's no affiliate link of any kind, there's no money involved.
summary: This news describes a tool or platform that helps users understand and run various large language models (LLMs) directly on different Apple devices. It provides simulations and an index to show which models are compatible with specific hardware, emphasizing offline functionality and privacy. Running LLMs locally is a growing trend, offering significant benefits like enhanced privacy, reduced costs (by avoiding API calls), and greater customizability. For you, understanding local deployment is crucial for developing privacy-centric applications, working in environments with limited internet access, or simply experimenting without incurring cloud costs. This is a very practical skill for full-stack and MLOps roles. You could try experimenting with running a small LLM locally on your own machine using frameworks like `llama.cpp` or Hugging Face's `transformers` library.
why: Running LLMs locally offers privacy, cost savings, and practical deployment experience.

title: How to Build a RAG Chatbot with n8n | Vector Database + AI Agent + OpenAI
author: AI for Librarians
raw_text: How do you build a chatbot that can answer questions from your own documents instead of relying only on an LLM's general ...
summary: this tutorial demonstrates how to build a retrieval-augmented generation (rag) chatbot that can answer questions using your own specific documents, rather than just relying on an llm's general knowledge. it uses n8n, a workflow automation tool, along with a vector database and an ai agent powered by openai. for you, this is a practical example of how to combine different components – a vector database for knowledge retrieval, an llm for generation, and an ai agent for orchestration – into a functional system. the use of n8n also gives you insight into mlops practices, showing how to automate and manage the workflow of such an application. consider exploring how n8n simplifies connecting various services to build your ai application.

title: Show HN: Run Google DataProc cluster on your local
author: jaysen_apache
raw_text:
Google does not provide official docker image for developers or AI agents to run dataproc cluster locally. so everybody need to spin up for even dev/CI testing,etc..now you or your AI agent can: 
docker run --rm agentcloud/dataproc:3.0.0-debian13 self-testsaves time and cost.it basically packages the same component version and make the hadoop and spark to developer.Here are docker images for other dataproc versions:https://hub.docker.com/r/agentcloud/dataproc/tagshere is full blog for more use-cases: https://local.cloud/blog/run-dataproc-locally-docker/
summary: This item introduces a docker image that lets you run a Google DataProc cluster locally on your machine. DataProc is Google Cloud's managed service for big data processing, primarily using Apache Hadoop and Spark. Traditionally, developing and testing applications for DataProc required spinning up a cloud cluster, which could be slow and costly for iterative development. This local solution provides a convenient way to simulate the DataProc environment, allowing you to develop, test, and debug your Spark and Hadoop jobs without cloud dependencies. It helps save time and money during the development and continuous integration phases. You could try pulling the docker image and running a basic spark word count example to see it in action.
why: Test big data pipelines locally, saving time and cloud costs.
